head: b7f9b47c9c0edb6d50a9b4c134ee9a235d95c077
title: Reduce sparse static token-presence storage eightfold
body:
## Change

Store SparseStaticEmbedding's dense token-presence mask as booleans and convert the incoming binary attention mask to that representation before scattering. Token presence is a binary value, but the current mask uses int64 and is retained by autograd for the weight gradient. Boolean storage reduces this retained mask from eight bytes to one byte per vocabulary entry. It also accepts boolean and uint8 attention masks without a scatter dtype error.

The weighted embeddings and residual addition retain their existing dtypes. This targets storage of token presence; #4184 separately addresses repeated-token scatter conflicts.

## Validation and memory measurement

The successful sparse-mask jobs in [this exact-base CPU run](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/actions/runs/43921700020) compare base `9ac7fdb4` and candidate `b7f9b47c` with PyTorch **2.6.0** and **2.14.1**. New tests produce **17 failures and 9 passes on base**: sixteen mask-dtype errors and one storage-size assertion. The candidate plus existing SparseStaticEmbedding tests produces **31 passes** in each environment. All pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass.

Coverage includes float16, bfloat16, float32 and float64 weights; int64, boolean and uint8 binary attention masks; residual embeddings; output and weight/residual gradients; and a complete locally constructed SparseEncoder training forward/backward.

The [reproducible benchmark](https://github.com/Afloat16/geoopt/blob/d52e86f7b80cc9c660026e6403c2b7e9d32ca901/.validation/st-sparse-static-mask-benchmark.py) uses a 32,768-token vocabulary and 128-token sequences. Saved-tensor hooks measure unique storage retained by the module's forward, rather than process RSS or the whole training graph. Output and weight-gradient SHA-256 digests match exactly before and after.

| Batch size | Before retained mask | After retained mask | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128 | 32 MiB | 4 MiB | 87.5% |
| 512 | 128 MiB | 16 MiB | 87.5% |

Five timed full module forward/backward repetitions after two warmups measured 46.96 → 45.01 ms and 359.46 → 307.06 ms on the PyTorch 2.14.1 CPU runner (1.04× and 1.17×). The separate 2.6.0 runner measured 1.08× and 1.15×. The main benefit is the deterministic eightfold reduction in retained mask storage.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex helped with investigation, implementation, regression tests and benchmarking.
